subject: A job offer you never applied for
preheader: A fake job scam, how to back up your photos, and a packing checklist from AI.
intro: Many of us are looking for extra income or a fresh start. Scammers know it. Here is what to watch for.

sections.label: Scam of the week
sections.title: The job offer that finds you first
paragraphs: A text or email says you got a job you never applied for. The pay sounds great, the work is easy, and they want to hire you right away. Often the "interview" happens only by chat.
Then comes the catch. They ask you to pay for equipment or training, to cash a check and send some of it back, or to share your bank or ID details for "payroll."
bullets: A real employer never asks you to pay money to get hired.
Never send back part of a check. The check can turn out to be fake after the money is gone.
Look up the company yourself and contact it through its own website. Do not use the contact details in the message.
Do not share ID or bank details before you have confirmed the job is real.

sections.label: Tip of the week
sections.title: Back up your photos
paragraphs: Phones get lost, dropped and replaced. Your photos should not go with them. A backup keeps a second copy in a safe place.
bullets: iPhone: open Settings, tap your name, then look for iCloud and Photos, and turn on the sync option.
Android: open the Google Photos app, tap your profile picture, then look for the backup option and turn it on.
Connect to Wi-Fi and plug in the phone while it makes the first copy. It can take a while.
sections.note: Menu names vary by phone and software version. If you cannot find it, search "backup" in Settings.

sections.label: AI trick of the week
sections.title: Make a checklist for any trip
paragraphs: Travel season is close. Tell AI where you are going and for how long, and ask for a packing checklist.
sections.prompt: Make a packing checklist for a 4-day winter visit to see family. We will drive, and I need to bring a few medications and a laptop. Group the list by category.
sections.note: Skim the list and cross off what you do not need. Never type passport or account numbers into an AI chat.
